sourcedFrom: Kimber MICRO™/MICRO 9™ Models — Safety & Instruction Manual — MICRO/MICRO 9 Manual, updated 2023 (2023)
cleanIntro: The Micro 9 is a scaled 1911, and the scaling is what bites: the recoil spring is short, stiff and genuinely under tension, and the thumb-safety plunger will leave the frame if you engage the safety with the slide off. Kimber's interval is after every use, and every six months even unused. Glasses on for this one — the book says so twice in the same section.

steps.title: Unload, and look into the magazine well AND the chamber
steps.action: Keep it pointed somewhere harmless, drop the magazine, and lock the slide back. Then look into both the magazine well and the chamber before anything else — a subcompact hides a round behind a short ejection port better than a full-size does.
steps.quote: Keeping the firearm pointed in a safe direction, unload the firearm (see pages 35-39) and visually inspect that the magazine well and chamber are empty.
steps.cite: Kimber MICRO™/MICRO 9™ Models — Safety & Instruction Manual — MICRO/MICRO 9 Manual, updated 2023 — Disassembly (field stripping), p.44

steps.title: ⛔ Never a finger on the trigger while loading or unloading
steps.action: Kimber puts this in capitals in its own manual, and on a single-action pistol with a cocked hammer it is not a formality.
steps.quote: NEVER TOUCH THE TRIGGER WHEN LOADING OR UNLOADING THE FIREARM.
steps.cite: Kimber MICRO™/MICRO 9™ Models — Safety & Instruction Manual — MICRO/MICRO 9 Manual, updated 2023 — Unloading, p.36

steps.title: Eye protection — the recoil spring is the reason
steps.action: Put glasses on before the slide stop moves. The book names the recoil spring specifically: it is under tension and it can leave the gun with enough force to injure you.
steps.quote: Exercise great caution as the recoil spring is under tension and can fly out with enough force to cause serious injury, property damage or loss.
steps.cite: Kimber MICRO™/MICRO 9™ Models — Safety & Instruction Manual — MICRO/MICRO 9 Manual, updated 2023 — Disassembly (field stripping), p.44

steps.title: Mini-Comp models only — T10 Torx, two screws, then twist it off
steps.action: If your Micro wears a threaded Mini-Comp, it comes off before the strip. Back both screws out counterclockwise with the supplied T10 Torx L-key and twist the comp off counterclockwise. Kimber recommends doing this with the slide still on the frame, which gives you something to hold.
steps.aside: It is recommended to have the slide assembled to the frame when removing and reinstalling the Mini-Comp.
steps.quote: To remove the Mini-Comp for field striping remove both screws at the bottom of the MiniComp by using the supplied T10 Torx L-Key turning the screws counterclockwise.
steps.cite: Kimber MICRO™/MICRO 9™ Models — Safety & Instruction Manual — MICRO/MICRO 9 Manual, updated 2023 — Removing Mini-Comp, p.52

steps.title: Cock the hammer, then line the tab up with the notch
steps.action: Cock the hammer and draw the slide back until the semi-circular tab on the back of the slide stop sits in the semicircular disassembly notch in the bottom of the slide. This is a feel-and-look step: too far back and the pin will not push, not far enough and it will not either.
steps.quote: Cock the hammer and move the slide toward the rear until the semi-circular tab on the back of the slide stop aligns with the semicircular disassembly notch in the bottom of the slide.
steps.cite: Kimber MICRO™/MICRO 9™ Models — Safety & Instruction Manual — MICRO/MICRO 9 Manual, updated 2023 — Disassembly (field stripping), p.44

steps.title: Push the pin in from the RIGHT, take the stop out LEFT
steps.action: Holding the slide exactly where it is, push inward on the protruding end of the slide stop pin on the right side, and draw the slide stop out of the left side. Directional — pushing from the wrong side just jams it.
steps.quote: Holding the slide in that position, push inward on the protruding end of the slide stop pin (on the right side of the slide) and remove the slide stop from the left side.
steps.cite: Kimber MICRO™/MICRO 9™ Models — Safety & Instruction Manual — MICRO/MICRO 9 Manual, updated 2023 — Disassembly (field stripping), p.45

steps.title: ⛔ Slide forward off the frame — and DO NOT touch the thumb safety now
steps.action: Run the slide assembly forward off the frame. From this moment until the slide is back on, the thumb safety stays down. Pushing it up with the slide off launches the detent plunger out of the frame under spring tension — one of the most common ways a Micro loses a part on a cleaning bench.
steps.aside: Once the slide is removed DO NOT engage the thumb safety into the “ON” position.
steps.quote: Slide the slide assembly forward and off the frame.
steps.cite: Kimber MICRO™/MICRO 9™ Models — Safety & Instruction Manual — MICRO/MICRO 9 Manual, updated 2023 — Disassembly (field stripping), p.45

steps.title: Recoil spring guide and spring — lift, then withdraw rearward
steps.action: Lift the guide assembly slightly and draw it out toward the rear of the slide. Keep a thumb over it as it comes; this is the tensioned part the eye-protection warning is about.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil spring guide and spring by lifting the assembly slightly, then withdrawing it toward the rear of the slide.
steps.cite: Kimber MICRO™/MICRO 9™ Models — Safety & Instruction Manual — MICRO/MICRO 9 Manual, updated 2023 — Disassembly (field stripping), p.45

steps.title: Spring off the guide rod without kinking it
steps.action: Slide the recoil spring off the guide rod, keeping it straight. A short stiff spring takes a permanent bend easily, and a bent recoil spring on a subcompact shows up as failures to return to battery.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil spring from the guide rod while being careful not to bend the spring.
steps.cite: Kimber MICRO™/MICRO 9™ Models — Safety & Instruction Manual — MICRO/MICRO 9 Manual, updated 2023 — Disassembly (field stripping), p.45

steps.title: Barrel out — lift first, then rearward
steps.action: Lift the barrel, then move it to the rear and out of the slide. Lifting is what clears the cam lug; trying to push it straight back binds it against the locking lugs.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel from the slide by first lifting, then moving the barrel to the rear out away from the slide.
steps.cite: Kimber MICRO™/MICRO 9™ Models — Safety & Instruction Manual — MICRO/MICRO 9 Manual, updated 2023 — Disassembly (field stripping), p.45

steps.title: Field strip complete — and that is the whole of it
steps.action: Slide, barrel, recoil spring, guide rod, frame. Kimber draws the line here explicitly and voids the warranty past it; no internal component gets manipulated beyond what the book instructs.
steps.quote: Do not manipulate any internal components beyond what you are instructed to do in this manual.
steps.cite: Kimber MICRO™/MICRO 9™ Models — Safety & Instruction Manual — MICRO/MICRO 9 Manual, updated 2023 — p.46

deepAbsentReason: ⛔ KIMBER PUBLISHES NO DEEPER PROCEDURE FOR THE MICRO AND FORBIDS ONE: disassembly beyond the field strip is out of bounds, internal components are not to be manipulated, and doing either voids the warranty. ⚠ FULL-SIZE 1911 BOOKS DO publish the steps this one stops short of — and none is borrowed, because this is a different gun in a smaller frame with its own detent plunger hazard.

cleaning.name: INTERVAL — after every use, and twice a year regardless
tasks: Clean after each use or any exposure to the elements
Clean and lubricate every six months even if it has not been fired
A carry gun collects lint and sweat without ever being shot
cleaning.quote: Kimber firearms should be cleaned after each use or exposure to the elements.
cleaning.src: Kimber MICRO™/MICRO 9™ Models — Safety & Instruction Manual, Cleaning, p.56

cleaning.name: BREECH FACE AND PARTS — nylon brush
tasks: Nylon brush or toothbrush on the breech face and around the extractor
Bore and chamber with solvent, then patches until clean
Barrel hood, cam lug and locking lugs — where a Micro carries its wear
⛔ Night sights never go near an ultrasonic cleaner
cleaning.quote: Clean the breech face and all parts (a toothbrush or similar nylon brush works well).
cleaning.src: Kimber MICRO™/MICRO 9™ Models — Safety & Instruction Manual, Cleaning, p.56

cleaning.name: ⛔ SOLVENT OUT OF THE FIRING PIN CHANNEL AND OFF THE BREECH FACE
tasks: No oil or solvent left in the firing pin channel
Nothing wet left on the breech face or inside the magazine
Never spray lubricant where it can reach cartridges
Oil in a primer is a misfire you will not see coming
cleaning.quote: do not allow oil or solvent to remain in the firing pin channel, on the breech face or inside the magazine
cleaning.src: Kimber MICRO™/MICRO 9™ Models — Safety & Instruction Manual, p.10

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION — oil, not grease, and by the drop
tasks: Premium light oil; grease is not recommended by Kimber
Slide and frame rails: 3 drops each side
Barrel hood 2 drops; each locking lug 1 drop; outside of barrel 3 drops
Disconnector 1 drop; slide stop pin 1 drop; guide rod 1 drop
Cocked hammer: 1 drop between hammer and frame
cleaning.src: Kimber MICRO™/MICRO 9™ Models — Safety & Instruction Manual, Lubrication, p.57

reassembly: Thumb safety still DOWN — it does not go up until the slide is home.
Barrel into the slide: cam lug facing upward, placed down and in.
Recoil spring onto the guide rod, seated against the base of the guide rod.
⛔ Round-wire spring with one open and one closed end: the CLOSED end goes on first.
Guide assembly into the slide from the rear.
Slide onto the frame, drawn back until the tab lines up with the disassembly notch.
Slide stop in from the left, pin pushed home from the right until flush.
Work the slide back and forth 5–6 times before you trust it.
fncheck: Magazine out, chamber checked by eye and finger. Rack the slide several times and confirm it returns fully to battery each time. With the hammer cocked and the slide forward, push the thumb safety fully up — it will not engage unless the hammer is cocked and the slide is fully forward, which is itself the test. Safety on, pull the trigger: no hammer fall. Safety off, trigger: it falls. ⛔ If the safety will only sit part-way, stop — an intermediate position can fire.
